Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

Ṭā-Sīn (طسۤ): This is one of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa). It is read: "Ṭā. Sīn."

Tilka (تلك): That is, the verses composed of these letters are verses of the Qur'an.

Hudan wa-bushrā (هدى وبشرى): That is, signposts of guidance to the straight path, and good tidings for those who are guided.

Zayyannā lahum aʿmālahum (زيّنا لهم أعمالهم): That is, We made them beloved to them, according to Our sunnah regarding those who do not believe in the Resurrection and the Recompense.

Fa-hum yaʿmahūn (فهم يعمهون): In far-reaching error and a bewilderment that never ends.

Lahum sūʾ al-ʿadhāb (لهم سوء العذاب): That is, in this world, through capture and killing.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted's saying ﴿Ṭā-Sīn﴾: We have already mentioned that the early generation (al-salaf) used to say about disjointed letters such as these: "God knows best what He means by them." This is the safest position. We also mentioned that there is a benefit that may be drawn from the indication by "tilka" or "dhālika": the miraculous Qur'an, with which its Revealer, the Mighty and Majestic, challenged humankind and jinn, is composed of letters of this kind, Arabic letters. So, O Arabs, compose a surah like it, or more. If you are unable, then believe that it is the speech of God and His revelation, and act upon what it contains and what it calls to.

And His saying ﴿Tilka āyātu al-Qurʾān﴾: That is, the verses of the Qur'an composed of letters like these. ﴿Wa-kitābin mubīn﴾: That is, clarifying everything that needs clarification of truth and law in all matters of life.

And His saying: ﴿Hudan wa-bushrā lil-muʾminīn﴾: That is, a guide to the straight path, which leads its follower to happiness and perfection in both abodes. ﴿Wa-bushrā﴾: That is, a great good news for the believers, meaning those who believe in God, in meeting Him, and in the Messenger and what he brought. ﴿Alladhīna yuqīmūna al-ṣalāh﴾: by performing it at its times, in the houses of God, with its conditions, pillars, obligations, sunan and etiquette fully observed. ﴿Wa-yu'tūna al-zakāh﴾: when it becomes obligatory upon them. ﴿Wa-hum bil-ākhirati hum yūqinūn﴾: that is, in the Last Abode, certain of its existence, of their return to it, and of what it contains of reckoning and recompense.

And the Exalted's saying: ﴿Inna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirah﴾: that is, do not believe in the Resurrection and the Recompense. ﴿Zayyannā lahum aʿmālahum﴾: that is, We made their deeds beloved to them so that they engage in them, and these are deeds of evil and corruption. This is according to Our sunnah regarding one who denies the Resurrection and becomes one who fears no reckoning and dreads no punishment; he plunges into vices and desires and no longer refrains from ugly deeds. ﴿Fa-hum﴾ because of that ﴿yaʿmahūn﴾: in their conduct they stumble about, not knowing what is good nor denouncing what is evil.

And the Exalted's saying: ﴿Ulāʾika alladhīna lahum sūʾ al-ʿadhāb﴾: that is, in this world, through capture and killing; and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers among all the people of the Fire, that is, the most severely punished.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The demonstration of the miraculousness of the Qur'an, since its verses are composed of letters like Ṭā-Sīn and Ḥā-Mīm, and the Arabs' inability to compose the like of it.

2- The Qur'an's being a guide and good tidings for believers who are committed to the requirements of faith.

3- Denying the Resurrection and the Hereafter makes its holder the worst of creation and in a state worse than dogs and pigs.

4- The obligation to fight atheists and to take them captive or kill them until they believe in God and in meeting Him, since they are a danger to themselves and to humanity alike.

**Explanation of the Words:**

**﴿وإنك لتلقى﴾ (wa-innaka la-tulaqqa):** that is, you receive it, memorize it, and are taught it.

**﴿من لدن حكيم﴾ (min ladun hakim):** that is, from the presence of a Wise, All-Knowing One, who is God, may His majesty be exalted.

**﴿آنست ناراً﴾ (ānastu nāran):** that is, I saw a fire from a distance, and from it I gained some comfort.

**﴿سآتيكم منها بخبر﴾ (sa-ātīkum minhā bi-khabar):** that is, concerning the way, since they had lost their path to Egypt in the desert.

**﴿بشهاب قبس﴾ (bi-shihāb qabas):** that is, a burning brand of fire taken from its source.

**﴿لعلكم تصطلون﴾ (la'allakum taṣṭalūn):** that is, that you may warm yourselves.

**﴿أن بورك من في النار﴾ (an būrika man fī al-nār):** that is, God, may His majesty be exalted, blessed the one in the fire, who is Moses, peace be upon him, since he was in the blessed place from which God Most High called out to Moses.

**﴿وسبحان الله رب العالمين﴾ (wa-subḥān Allāh rabb al-ʿālamīn):** that is, the Lord Most High declared Himself free of whatever is unbefitting His majesty and perfection, such as the attributes of created things.

**﴿يا موسى إنه أنا الله﴾ (yā Mūsā innahu anā Allāh):** that is, the matter is that I am God, the Mighty, the Wise, who called to you and blessed you.

**﴿تهتز كأنها جان﴾ (tahtazz ka'annahā jān):** that is, it moves swiftly, as though it were a serpent, light and quick.

**﴿ولم يعقب﴾ (wa-lam yuʿaqqib):** that is, he did not return to it, out of fear and terror of it.

**﴿ثم بدل حسناً بعد سوء﴾ (thumma baddala ḥasanan baʿda sū'):** that is, he repented and did righteous deeds after the wrong that had occurred from him.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The context still concerns affirming the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). God Most High's words, ﴿And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from the presence of One Wise and All-Knowing﴾, inform His Messenger that he is being given and taught and made to memorize the Qur'an by a Wise One in His governance and All-Knowing of His creation, who is God, may His majesty be glorified and His authority exalted.

His words, ﴿When Moses said﴾, mean: mention to those who deny revelation and reject your prophethood when Moses said… Would such a thing happen without receiving from God Most High? The answer is no. Therefore you are truly and genuinely the Messenger of God. ﴿When Moses said to his family﴾, that is, his wife and children, ﴿"I have seen a fire; I will bring you news from it or bring you a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves"﴾, that is, I saw it while seeking comfort from it, since they were on a cold winter night and had lost their way.

His words, ﴿When he came to it﴾, that is, the fire, ﴿he was called﴾, that is, his Lord called him saying: ﴿Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it﴾, that is, sanctified is the one in the fire, which is the light of God, may His majesty be exalted, and that is Moses, peace be upon him, and whoever is around it from the sacred land of Jerusalem and Syria. God knows best what He intends by His speech. We ask Him for forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance if we fail to grasp His intended meaning in His speech and address. O God, forgive our sin and have mercy on our weakness and frailty, for You are Forgiving and Merciful.

His words, ﴿And glory be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, declare that He is free of whatever is unbefitting His majesty and perfection.

His words, ﴿O Moses, indeed, it is I, God, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, mean: the One who is calling to you is God, the Possessor of divinity over His creation, the Mighty, the Victorious, whom none can prevent from His will, the Wise in His decree, His governance, and His management of His dominion. After He made Himself known to him and removed the fear from his soul, He commanded him to throw down his staff, to train him in using it. So He said, ﴿And throw down your staff﴾. He threw it down, and it moved swiftly like a serpent, ﴿and when he saw it moving as though it were a snake, he turned and fled without looking back﴾, that is, he retreated backward in terror and fear. ﴿And he did not return﴾, that is, he did not come back to it out of fear of it. Then his Lord called to him: ﴿O Moses, do not fear; indeed, the messengers do not fear in My presence﴾. ﴿Except one who has wronged﴾, that is, wronged himself by committing a sin. Such a person does fear, but if he repents after the sin and does good deeds after bad ones, then he need not fear, for I am Forgiving and Merciful, so I will forgive him and have mercy on him.

God Most High reassured the soul of Moses with this, because Moses was aware that he had committed a sin by killing the Copt before his prophethood and mission. Although the killing was accidental, it still required expiation: freeing a slave or fasting two consecutive months.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. Affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad.
2. The permissibility of travelling with one's family and children, and the possibility of losing one's way even for prophets and the intelligent.
3. The guardianship (qawwamah) of men over women and children.
4. God Most High's manifestation to Moses in the blessed place, His communion with him, and His training of him in the staff and the means by which he would later confront Pharaoh and his chiefs.
5. Wrongdoing causes fear and punishment, except for one who repents and reforms, for God is Forgiving and Merciful.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 15–19:

Explanation of the words:

ʿIlm (knowledge): this is knowledge of what was not given to others, such as knowing the language of birds, alongside knowledge of the Sharia such as judgment and the like.

Wa-qalā al-ḥamdu lillāh (And they both said, "Praise be to God"): that is, thanks to Him.

ʿAlā kathīrin min ʿibādihi al-muʾminīn (above many of His believing servants): that is, with prophethood and the subjugation of jinn, humans and devils.

Wa-waritha Sulaymān Dāwūd (And Solomon inherited David): that is, he inherited his father after his death in prophethood, kingship and knowledge, to the exclusion of his other children.

ʿUllimnā manṭiq al-ṭayr (We have been taught the speech of birds): that is, understanding the sounds of birds and what they say when they chirp.

Wa-ūtīnā min kulli shayʾ (And we have been given of all things): what others among the prophets and kings were given.

Wa-ḥushira li-Sulaymān junūduhu (And there were gathered for Solomon his hosts): that is, his soldiers of jinn, humans and birds were assembled for him on a march.

Fa-hum yūzaʿūn (and they were marshalled): that is, they were driven along and their first ranks were held back until the last joined them, so that they proceeded in order.

Lā yaḥṭimannakum Sulaymān (Let not Solomon and his hosts crush you): that is, let them not crush and kill you.

Wa-hum lā yashʿurūn (while they do not perceive): that is, of you.

Awziʿnī an ashkura (Inspire me to be grateful): that is, inspire me and grant me success to be thankful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the accounts of David and Solomon, peace be upon them, mentioned after He, exalted is He, informed that He instructs His Messenger Muhammad and teaches him from His own presence, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. He demonstrated this with a summary of the story of Moses, peace be upon him, then mentioned another proof, the story of David and Solomon. He said, exalted is He, ﴿And We certainly gave﴾, that is, We gave David and Solomon ﴿knowledge﴾, that is, the father and the son, a special knowledge such as knowing the speech of birds, making coats of mail and softening iron, in addition to the knowledge of the Sharia and judgment. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And they both said, "Praise be to God"﴾, that is, they thanked their Lord by their saying ﴿"Praise be to God"﴾, that is, thanks belong to God who has favoured us above many of His believing servants with what He gave them of special qualities and bounties. This is what the first verse [14] indicates. As for the second verse [15], He, exalted is He, informed in it that Solomon inherited his father David alone, to the exclusion of his other children, and that was in prophethood and kingship, not in dirhams, dinars, sheep or camels, because prophets do not bequeath; what they leave is charity. He also informed that Solomon said among the people, ﴿O people, we have been taught the speech of birds﴾, so no bird chirps but he knows what it is saying in its chirping, ﴿and we have been given of all things﴾ that others were given of prophethood, kingship, knowledge and wisdom. ﴿Indeed, this is evidently the clear bounty﴾, that is, the manifest, evident bounty of God, exalted is He. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And there were gathered for Solomon his hosts﴾, that is, his hosts were assembled for him ﴿of the jinn and mankind and birds, and they were marshalled﴾ is a report of a march that Solomon undertook with his army. ﴿And they were marshalled﴾, that is, his hosts were driven along in order, so that some did not get ahead of others, and its first was held back until its last joined, to maintain order in the march. They continued marching in this manner until they came upon the valley of the ants in al-Sham, and an ant said, ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you while they do not perceive﴾. She said this out of compassion and pity for females of her own kind, teaching humankind compassion, pity and counsel for their own kind, if they only knew. And she excused Solomon and his army by her saying, "while they do not perceive you", for otherwise they would not have trampled you and walked over you so as to crush you.

As soon as Solomon heard her and understood her speech, he smiled laughing at her saying. ﴿And he said, "My Lord"﴾, that is, O Lord, ﴿"inspire me"﴾, that is, inspire me ﴿"to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteous deeds with which You are pleased"﴾, that is, and facilitate for me a righteous deed with which You are pleased from me. ﴿"And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants"﴾, that is, among their number in the Abode of Peace.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of thanking God for blessings.

2- Solomon's inheritance from David was not in wealth, because prophets do not bequeath, but was in prophethood and kingship.

3- The sign of God teaching Solomon the speech of birds and subjecting the jinn and devils to him.

4- The virtue of the ant over many creatures appeared in the ant's counsel to her sisters and her compassion for them.

5- The intelligence and shrewdness of the ant, which made Solomon laugh in wonder at it.

6- The obligation of thanks upon witnessing a blessing and seeing God's bounty, mighty and majestic is He.

7- Confirmation of Muhammad's prophethood, since such an account cannot come to him except through divine revelation.

4- The virtue of the ant over many creatures appeared in the ant's counsel to her sisters and her compassion for them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 20–26:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-tafaqqada al-tayr (وتفقد الطير): i.e., he inspected the birds and looked over them.

Mali la ara al-hudhud (مالي لا أرى الهدهد): Present to me what prevented me from seeing it, or was it among the absent?

La-u'adhdhabannahu 'adhaban shadidan (لأعذبنه عذاباً شديداً): i.e., by plucking out its feathers and casting it into the sun so that it would not be protected from vermin.

Bi-sultanin mubin (بسلطان مبين): i.e., with a clear proof of its excuse for its absence.

Fa-makatha ghayra ba'id (فمكث غير بعيد): i.e., for a short time; and Sulayman came humbly.

Ahatu bima lam tuhit bihi (أحطت بما لم تحط به): i.e., I have learned what you have not learned.

Wa-ji'tuka min Saba' (وجئتك من سبأ): Saba' is a tribe from the tribes of Yemen.

Inni wajadtu imra'atan (إني وجدت امرأة): she is Bilqis the queen.

Wa-laha 'arshun 'azim (ولها عرش عظيم): i.e., a great throne.

Fa-sadahum 'ani al-sabil (فصدهم عن السبيل): i.e., from the path of truth and guidance.

Alla yasjudu li-Allah (ألا يسجدوا لله): its original form is an yasjudu, meaning they do not follow guidance to prostrate to Allah. The "la" (لا) was added, and the nun was assimilated into it, so it became alla (ألاَّ), similar to the usage in "li-alla ya'lama ahl al-kitab" (لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب) at the end of surah al-Hadid.

Yukhriju al-khab'a fi al-samawat (يخرج الخبأ في السماوات): i.e., what is hidden in the heavens, such as rain, and on the earth, such as plants, and the earth.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the stories of Sulayman, peace be upon him, in the words of the Most High: ﴿And he inspected the birds﴾, i.e., Sulayman inspected his army of birds, seeking the hoopoe for a matter that occurred to him, namely as he was preparing for an important journey. He did not find it, so he said what Allah the Most High reported about him: ﴿Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or was it among the absent?﴾ Is there some obstacle that prevented me from seeing it? ﴿Or was it among the absent?﴾ i.e., rather, it was among the absent. ﴿I will surely punish it with a severe punishment﴾ by plucking its feathers and leaving it for vermin to devour, so that it cannot defend itself from them. ﴿Or I will surely slaughter it﴾ by cutting its throat, ﴿or it will bring me a clear authority﴾, i.e., a clear proof of the reason for its absence. The words of the Most High in verse [21]: ﴿So it remained﴾, i.e., the hoopoe, ﴿not long﴾, i.e., for a short time, and it came and said, humbly, lifting its neck and lowering its tail and wings: ﴿I have encompassed [knowledge] of that which you have not encompassed﴾, i.e., I have learned what you have not learned. ﴿And I have come to you from Saba' with certain news﴾. Saba' is a tribe from the tribes of Yemen, and "certain news" is true information about which there is no doubt. It then began to explain the content of the news, saying: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman﴾, who is Bilqis, ﴿ruling them, and she has been given of all things﴾, i.e., of the means of strength and the manifestations of sovereignty, ﴿and she has a great throne﴾, i.e., the seat of her kingship upon which she sits, described as great because it is adorned with jewels and gold. His words ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah﴾ inform first about their worldly conditions and second about their religious conditions. His words ﴿and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them﴾, i.e., their false, polytheistic deeds, ﴿and averted them﴾ by that ﴿from the way﴾, i.e., the way of guidance and truth; therefore they are not guided to prostrate to Allah, ﴿who brings out what is hidden﴾, i.e., the hidden thing; this is the use of the verbal noun in the sense of the passive participle, ﴿in the heavens﴾, such as rain, ﴿and the earth﴾, such as plants. He, glory be to Him, knows what they conceal in their souls and what they declare with their tongues. ﴿Allah – there is no deity but Him, Lord of the Great Throne.﴾

The description of the Lord, the Most High, as "Lord of the Great Throne" is set against Bilqis's description of her throne, and how could the throne of a created being, even if she is a queen and daughter of a king named Sharahil, compare with the throne of Allah, the Creator of all things and Owner of all things?

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of reviewing armies and inspecting the conditions of the subjects.

2- The legitimacy of disciplining one who disobeys the ruler without a lawful excuse.

3- The legitimacy of employing reconnaissance aircraft and studying the geography of the world.

4- The fulfillment of the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "A people will never prosper who entrust their affairs to a woman," since Sulayman soon overcame them.

5- The statement that there were those who worshipped the sun, since prostrating to it is worship.

6- The statement that the one most deserving of worship is Allah, there is no deity but Him, Lord of the Great Throne.

7- The legitimacy of prostration for one who recites this verse or hears its recitation: ﴿Allah – there is no deity but Him, Lord of the Great Throne﴾.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 27–31:

Explanation of the words:

*Sananzuru ash-sadaqta am kunta min al-kadhibin* (﴿We shall see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars﴾): that is, after We have tested you.

*Fa-alqihi ilayhim* (﴿Then deliver it to them﴾): that is, to the men of the palace who were in the seat of judgement.

*Thumma tawalla anhum* (﴿then withdraw from them﴾): that is, step aside and conceal yourself, staying out of their sight.

*Fa-anzur madha yarji'un* (﴿and see what they return with in reply﴾): that is, what some of them say to one another concerning the letter.

*Ya ayyuha al-mala'* (﴿O chiefs﴾): that is, O nobles of the land, its notables, and those who bind and loose its affairs.

*Ilqiya ilayya kitabun karim* (﴿A noble letter has been delivered to me﴾): that is, the hoopoe dropped it into her lap.

*Alla ta'lu 'alayya* (﴿that you not exalt yourselves against me﴾): that is, do not be arrogant out of submission to the self and its desires.

*Wa'tuni muslimin* (﴿and come to me in submission﴾): that is, obedient and humbled.

The meaning of the verses:

﴿He said, "We shall see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars."﴾ That is, Solomon said to the hoopoe, after the hoopoe had presented its argument for its absence: "We shall see by testing you, whether you spoke the truth in what you claimed and stated, or whether you were among the liars." He then began the test: he wrote a letter, sealed it, and said to it: ﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them﴾, that is, step aside and hide yourself from them, ﴿and see what they return with in reply﴾ concerning the letter, that is, what some of them say to others about it. The hoopoe did as commanded: it took the letter, entered the palace through a window in it, and dropped the letter into the lap of Queen Bilqis. She was alarmed by it, read it, and then said, ﴿O chiefs, a noble letter has been delivered to me﴾, addressing the nobles of her people. She described it as noble because of the noble phrases it contained, and because it was sealed, and the seal is part of a letter's nobility. The text of the letter was as follows: [From Solomon, son of Dawud, to Bilqis, queen of Sheba. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission.]

Its content is what the queen stated in her words: ﴿It is from Solomon, and it reads: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission."﴾ As for "it is from Solomon", that means it issues from him and is written and sent by him. "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" means by His permission and His law. "Do not exalt yourselves against me" means do not be arrogant toward the truth, for I summon you in the name of Allah. "Come to me in submission" means humbled and obedient.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The legitimacy of testing and investigating an accused person.
2. The legitimacy of a ruler employing members of his subjects for the sake of the employer's needs.
3. The legitimacy of sending spies to learn the conditions of the enemy and what is happening among them.
4. The legitimacy of writing "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" in important letters and books, since it indicates the oneness of Allah, that He is Most Gracious and Most Merciful, and that the writer writes by Allah's permission to do so.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 32–35:

Explanation of the words:

"Aftūnī fī amrī" (advise me regarding my affair): explain to me the right course and what must be done about it.

"Mā kuntu qāti'atan amran" (I would not decide a matter): i.e., I would not render a judgment on it.

"Ḥattā tashhadūn" (until you attend): i.e., you attend me and state your opinion on it.

"Wa-ulū baʾsin shadīd" (and possessors of great might): i.e., possessors of tremendous material strength and of severe valour in war.

"Idhā dakhalū qaryatan" (when they enter a town): i.e., a city and the seat of a king.

"Afsadūhā" (they corrupt it): i.e., they lay it waste when they enter it by force, without reconciliation.

"Wa-kadhālika yafʿalūn" (and thus they do): i.e., just as I have mentioned to you, so do the senders of this letter act.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the account of the palace of Queen Bilqīs, and here she says to the men of her state what Allah, the Exalted, relates of her words: ﴿She said: "O chiefs, advise me in my affair. I would not decide any matter until you attend me."﴾ That is, advise me with whatever you see as sound. ﴿I would not decide a matter﴾ i.e., I would not issue a final judgment on it. ﴿Until you attend me﴾ i.e., you attend me and state your viewpoint on it. Her men answered her with what Allah, the Exalted, reports of them: ﴿They said: "We are possessors of strength﴾ in military terms, of weapons, equipment and experience ﴿and possessors of severe might﴾ when we engage in battles. ﴿But the command is yours, so consider what you will command﴾ — so order us, and we will carry out your command; we are at your disposal.

She answered them with what Allah, the Exalted, relates of her: ﴿She said: "Indeed, when kings enter a town﴾ i.e., a city by force, without reconciliation. ﴿They corrupt it﴾ i.e., they wreck its landmarks and alter and change its character, ﴿and make the most honoured of its people humble﴾ by striking and humiliating them and removing them from their posts. ﴿And thus﴾ the people of this letter ﴿do﴾ ﴿And indeed, I am sending them a gift, and I will see with what the envoys return﴾ i.e., with what the messengers we send return, whether they accept the gift or reject it, and in light of that we will act. If they accept the material gift, they are people of this world; if they reject it, they are people of religion, and then we will take what is necessary concerning them. There is no doubt that this gift was lavish and precious.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the principle of consultation (shūrā) in governance.

2- The permissibility of giving one's opinion sincerely and with integrity, and then leaving the matter to its people.

3- The permissibility of preparing equipment, providing weapons, and training men to bear and use them.

4- The entry of a hostile, victorious enemy into a land by force is dangerous, so the matter should be averted by reconciliation.

5- The demonstration of Queen Bilqīs's good statecraft, shrewdness and intelligence, and for this reason she inherited her father's throne.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 27, verses 36–40**

**Explanation of the words:**

﴿فلما جاء سليمان﴾: i.e., the envoy of the Queen, who was carrying the gift, along with his companions.

﴿فما آتاني الله خير مما آتاكم﴾: He gave me prophethood and kingship, and that is better than what He has given you, which is only wealth.

﴿بهديتكم تفرحون﴾: Because of your love of this world and your desire for its adornments.

﴿ارجع إليهم﴾: i.e., with the gift you have brought.

﴿بجنود لا قبل لهم بها﴾: i.e., they have no power to fight them.

﴿ولنخرجنهم منها﴾: i.e., from their city of Saba' (Sheba), which is named after a man called Saba'.

﴿أذلة وهم صاغرون﴾: i.e., if they do not come to me as Muslims, meaning submissive and subdued.

﴿قبل أن يأتوني مسلمين﴾: For I have the right to seize it before they come to me as Muslims, not after.

﴿قال عفريت من الجن﴾: i.e., a strong jinn, for the strong, powerful one among the jinn is called an ʿifrīt.

﴿قبل أن تقوم من مقامك﴾: i.e., from the seat of your judgment, which lasts from morning until noon.

﴿وإني عليه لقوي أمين﴾: i.e., strong enough to carry it, and trustworthy regarding what is in it of jewels and other things.

﴿وقال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب﴾: i.e., Sulayman (peace be upon him).

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with Sulayman (peace be upon him) and the Queen of Saba'. When she sent her gift, she was testing him to see whether he was a man of this world who accepts wealth, or a man of religion, so that she could act in light of what she knew of Sulayman's inclination. So when Sulayman received it, the Queen's envoy came to him with men carrying the gift. He said to them, as Allah the Exalted related about them in His words: ﴿Do you provide me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you﴾, meaning He gave me prophethood, knowledge, wisdom and kingship, and this is better than the wealth He gave you. ﴿Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift﴾, because of your love for this world and your desire for its adornments. He said to the Queen's envoy: ﴿Return to them﴾, i.e., with the gift you brought, and inform them that if they do not come to me as Muslims, ﴿then we will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist﴾, i.e., they have no power to fight them, ﴿and we will surely drive them out from it﴾, i.e., from their city of Saba', ﴿humbled, and they will be subdued﴾, i.e., submissive and obedient.

Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) said to the nobles of his realm and the notables of his lands: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ For I will not take it except before they come to me as Muslims, not after. Then a jinn ʿifrīt spoke, saying what Allah related about him: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾, i.e., from your seat of judgment, which usually ends around midday. ﴿And indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾, i.e., able to carry it and bring it within the time you have set, and trustworthy regarding what is in it of jewels and gold, none of which will be lost. Here ﴿the one who had knowledge from the Scripture said﴾, and he was Sulayman (peace be upon him): ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾. Open your eyes and look; your glance will not return to you before the throne is in front of you. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 41–44:

Explanation of the words:

"Qala nakkiru laha 'arshaha" (He said: Disguise her throne for her): i.e., alter its form and shape so that it is recognized only with difficulty.

"Atahtadi" (Will she be guided?): i.e., to recognizing it.

"Ahakadha 'arshuka" (Is your throne like this?): they made it confusing for her, for had they said, "This is your throne," she would have said, "Yes."

"Qalat ka'annahu huwa" (She said: It is as if it were it): so they confused her, and she said, "It is as if it were it."

"Wa sadda-ha ma kanat ta'budu min duni Allah" (And what she used to worship besides God had barred her): i.e., what she used to worship besides God turned her away from worshipping God, despite her knowledge and intelligence.

"Idkhuli al-sarh" (Enter the palace-court): i.e., the courtyard (bahw) of the sarh (sarh: a lofty palace). In its courtyard there was a large pool of water covered by a glass roof, which looks as if it were water.

"Fakashafat 'an saqayha" (So she uncovered her shins): thinking she was entering water she would walk through, so she lifted her garments.

"Hasibathu lujjah" (She thought it was a deep expanse): i.e., of water, a flowing body of water.

"Sarhun mumarradun min qawarir" (A palace smoothed with glass): i.e., made smooth of glass.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the conversations that took place between Solomon, peace be upon him, and Bilqis, the Queen of Sheba. She had set out in her royal procession after taking every precaution regarding her throne. However, the throne arrived before her by the invocation of one who had knowledge of the Book. Before her arrival, Solomon wished to test her mind in terms of sharpness or weakness, so he ordered his men to alter her throne by adding and removing parts, so that it would be recognized only with difficulty, as he, peace be upon him, said: ﴿We shall see whether she will be guided﴾ to recognizing it, ﴿or whether she will be among those who are not guided﴾ due to the weakness of their minds. When she came, ﴿it was said: Is your throne like this?﴾ They confused her with the alteration and with the wording, for it should have been said to her, "This is your throne." From this she perceived their trickery, ﴿she said: It is as if it were it﴾, for if she had said, "It is it," they would have said, "How can it be it when the distance is a two-month journey?" And if she had said, "It is not it," it would have been said to her, "How do you not recognize your own throne?" So she was endowed with intelligence and cunning. Hence Solomon, when he was impressed by her intelligence, said: ﴿And we were given the knowledge before her, and we were Muslims﴾, praising God and extolling Him within the statement he made.

His saying ﴿And what she used to worship besides God had barred her﴾ refers to her following her people, for they used to worship the sun besides God. ﴿Indeed she was of a disbelieving people﴾: this is the reason for her not believing and not monotheizing, which is what her people were upon.

Solomon sat in the courtyard of his palace, and beneath the courtyard was a great pool of water in which were many fish, and the water had waves; the roof of the pool was smoothed glass. With Solomon were his soldiers of humans and jinn, surrounding him and encircling him from every side. She was commanded to enter the palace because Solomon the king was calling her. ﴿When she saw it, she thought it was a deep expanse﴾ of water, ﴿and she uncovered her shins﴾. Then Solomon said to her, ﴿Indeed it is a palace smoothed with glass﴾, i.e., made smooth, ﴿of glass﴾, crystalline. Here, with the scene having overwhelmed her and her realizing that she had been misguided and wrongdoing, she spoke, saying: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, and thereby she became a Muslim and a righteous woman. The Qur'an mentions nothing further about her, so let us remain silent about what the Qur'an has kept silent about.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 45–49:

Explanation of the words:

*An u'budu* (that worship): i.e., that you worship Allah.

*Fariqan yakhtasimun* (two groups disputing): i.e., two groups, a believing monotheist group and a disbelieving polytheist group, dispute.

*Tasta'jiluna bi's-sayyi'ah* (you seek to hasten evil): i.e., you demand the punishment before mercy.

*Lawla tastaghfirun Allah* (why do you not seek forgiveness from Allah): i.e., why do you not seek forgiveness from your Lord by repenting to Him?

*Qalu ittayyarna bika* (they said, "We see an omen in you"): i.e., we consider you and those with you, the believing followers, to be a bad omen.

*Qala ta'irukum 'inda Allah* (he said, "Your omen is with Allah"): i.e., what you consider ill omens from birds, due to the hardships that befall you, is with Allah, whose knowledge it is.

*Bal antum qawmun tuftanun* (rather, you are a people being tested): i.e., you are being tested with good and evil.

*Tis'atu rahT* (nine men): i.e., nine men who were wrongdoers.

*Taqasamu bi'llah* (swear to one another by Allah): i.e., make oaths to one another by Allah, each one asking the other to swear to him.

*Lanubayyitannahu wa-ahlahu* (we will surely attack him and his family by night): i.e., we will surely kill him and those who believe in him, at night.

*Ma shahidna mahlaka ahlihi* (we did not witness the destruction of his family): i.e., we were not present at his killing, nor at the killing of his family.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, exalted is He, *"Wa-laqad arsalna"* (And We had certainly sent): this is the beginning of the account of the Prophet Salih, peace be upon him, with his people Thamud. When Allah mentioned the story of Sulayman with Bilqis, He mentioned the story of Salih with Thamud, to affirm the prophethood of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and to set before the polytheists of Quraysh historical events that represent their own situation with their Prophet, so that perhaps they would remember and believe. Allah, exalted is He, said, *"Wa-laqad arsalna ila Thamuda"* (And We had certainly sent to Thamud), i.e., the tribe of Thamud, *"akhahum"* (their brother), i.e., in lineage, *"Salihan an u'budu"* (Salih, [saying], "Worship"), i.e., he said to them, "Worship Allah," i.e., make Him one, *"fa-idha hum fariqan"* (then suddenly they were two groups), believers in monotheism and polytheists, *"yakhtasimun"* (disputing). One group calls to the worship of Allah alone, and another group calls to the worship of idols alongside Allah. It is the nature of opposition that it gives rise to dispute, each group wanting to defeat the other group. They asked Salih for signs and said, *"Fa'tina bima ta'iduna"* (Bring us what you threaten us with) [al-A'raf: 70], i.e., of punishment, *"in kunta mina as-sadiqin"* (if you are of the truthful) [al-A'raf: 70], in that you are a messenger to us like the messengers. He answered them and said, *"Ya qawmi lima tasta'jiluna bi's-sayyi'ah"* (O my people, why do you seek to hasten the evil), i.e., you demand of me your punishment, *"qabla al-hasanah"* (before the good). It was required that you ask for the good, which is mercy, and not for the evil, which is punishment. Your disbelief and your sins are the path to your punishment, just as your faith and obedience are the path to your salvation and happiness. So hasten to faith and obedience, seeking the good of this world and the Hereafter. By your disbelief and sins you are hastening your punishment. *"Lawla"* (why not), i.e., *"tastaghfirun Allah"* (do you not seek forgiveness from Allah) by abandoning polytheism and sins, *"la'allakum turhamun"* (so that perhaps you may be shown mercy), i.e., so that you may be shown mercy after this admonition and guidance. The people's answer was what Allah reported about them in His saying, *"Qalu ittayyarna bika wa-bi-man ma'aka"* (They said, "We see an omen in you and those with you"), i.e., we consider you and your believing followers to be an ill omen. He answered them with His saying, *"Ta'irukum 'inda Allah"* (Your omen is with Allah), i.e., what you consider ill omens from birds, due to the hardships that befall you, is with Allah, whose knowledge it is, and it will certainly occur; the matter is not one of ill omen or good omen, *"bal antum qawmun tuftanun"* (rather, you are a people being tested).

His saying, exalted is He, *"Wa-kana fi al-madinati tis'atu rahtin"* (And there were in the city nine men): i.e., in the city of al-Hijr, the Hijr of Thamud, nine men, *"yufsidun fi al-ard"* (who spread corruption in the land) by disbelief and sins, *"wa-la yuslihun"* (and did not reform). They are the ones who conspired to hamstring the she-camel, and among them was Qudar ibn Salif, who undertook to hamstring the she-camel.

These nine men said to one another in a private gathering, *"Taqasamu bi'llah"* (Swear to one another by Allah), i.e., let each one of you say, "By Allah," *"lanubayyitannahu"* (we will surely attack him at night), i.e., Salih, *"wa-ahlahu"* (and his family), i.e., his followers. That is, we will go to them and kill them at night. Then in the morning, *"lanaqulanna li-waliyyihi"* (we will surely say to his heir), i.e., to the blood-avenger of Salih from among his relatives, *"wa-Allah ma shahidna mahlaka ahlihi"* (by Allah, we did not witness the destruction of his family), nor his destruction, *"wa-inna la-sadiqun"* (and indeed we are truthful), in what we swear regarding our not having witnessed the destruction of Salih or the destruction of his companions.

Guidance of the verses:

1. Affirmation of the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ).

2. Affirmation of the fact that the conflict between truth and falsehood does not end until falsehood ends.

3. The prohibition of taking omens of ill fortune, and likewise of taking omens of good fortune; the Lawgiver permitted only optimism (tafa'ul) and nothing else.

4. Acting in disobedience to Allah, exalted is He, is corruption on the earth, and acting in obedience to Him is reform on the earth.

5. Affirmation that the polytheists believe in Allah, which is why they swear by Him, yet this did not admit them into Islam, because they associate with Allah in worship others among His creatures.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Wa-makarū makran*: they devised a hidden plot to kill Salih and the believers.

*Wa-makarnā makran*: and We devised a hidden plan to save Salih and the believers and to destroy the wrongdoers.

*Wa-hum lā yash'urūn*: without perceiving that We were planning their destruction.

*Buyūtuhum khāwiyah*: their houses are empty, with no one in them.

*Bimā ẓalamū*: because of their wrongdoing, which was shirk (associating partners with God) and sins.

*La-āyah*: a sign, or lesson.

*Wa-anjaynā alladhīna āmanū*: and We saved Salih and the believers.

**The meaning of the verses:**

God says, ﴿And they devised a plot﴾. This is the end of the story of Salih with Thamud. It has already been mentioned that nine men from Salih's people swore an oath together to ambush Salih and the believers and kill them at night, so that in their view they could prevent the punishment that Salih had promised them, which would descend upon them after three days. Their plan was carried out when they came to Salih while he was praying in a mosque of his beneath the mountain. A rock fell on them from the mountain and destroyed them all. Thus God plotted against them while they were unaware of it. Then God destroyed the whole people with the Blast, and they were found lying dead in their homes. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿So see what was the end of their scheme﴾, that is: look, O Our Messenger, at how that scheme ended and what its outcome was. ﴿That We destroyed them and their people, all of them.﴾ ﴿So those are their houses, empty because of their wrongdoing﴾, that is, because they wronged themselves through shirk and wronged Salih and the believers.

God's words, ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in the destruction of the nine men and of all of Thamud, ﴿is a sign﴾, that is, a proof of God's power, His knowledge, and His excellent management, ﴿for a people who know﴾, since they are the ones who see the sign and comprehend it.

God's words, ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be wary﴾, refer to Salih and the believers who had faith in God as their Lord and God, and in Salih as a prophet and messenger. Throughout their lives they guarded themselves against God's punishment by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger in what he commanded and forbade.

**Lessons from the verses:**

1. Establishing the principle: ﴿And the evil scheme does not encompass except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].
2. Establishing that the dwellings of wrongdoers end in ruin, for wrongdoing leaves the dwellings desolate.
3. Establishing that faith and God-consciousness (taqwa) are the cause of salvation, because God's protection of His servant is secured through them.

This is the meaning of His words, ﴿So see what was the end of their scheme﴾, that is: look, O Our Messenger, at how that scheme ended and what its outcome was. ﴿That We destroyed them and their people, all of them.﴾ ﴿So those are their houses, empty because of their wrongdoing﴾, that is, because they wronged themselves through shirk and wronged Salih and the believers.

God's words, ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in the destruction of the nine men and of all of Thamud, ﴿is a sign﴾, that is, a proof of God's power, His knowledge, and His excellent management, ﴿for a people who know﴾, since they are the ones who see the sign and comprehend it.

God's words, ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be wary﴾, refer to Salih and the believers who had faith in God as their Lord and God, and in Salih as a prophet and messenger. Throughout their lives they guarded themselves against God's punishment by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger in what he commanded and forbade.

**Lessons from the verses:**

1. Establishing the principle: ﴿And the evil scheme does not encompass except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].
2. Establishing that the dwellings of wrongdoers end in ruin, for wrongdoing leaves the dwellings desolate.
3. Establishing that faith and God-consciousness (taqwa) are the cause of salvation, because God's protection of His servant is secured through them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 54–55:

Explanation of the words:

Lut (Lot): That is, "Recall, for your people, Lut when he said to his people."

To his people: They were the inhabitants of the cities of Amurah (Gomorrah) and Sodom.

Al-fahisha (the abominable deed): That is, the foul trait, extremely foul in its ugliness, which is sodomy (liwat).

And you see: That is, while they were committing it in their assemblies openly, in full view, without concealment or screen.

Qawm tajhalun (a people who are ignorant): That is, ignorant of how ugly what you do is and of the shame and punishment that follow from it.

Meaning of the two verses:

This is the beginning of the account of Lut, peace be upon him, with his people, the people of Lut. Allah the Exalted says, ﴿And Lut﴾, meaning: and mention, just as you mentioned Salih and his people, mention Lut ﴿when he said to his people﴾, rebuking them and reproaching them for their monstrous deed: ﴿Do you commit the abomination while you see [it]?﴾, meaning: its ugliness and heinousness, with your insight and with your eyes, since they used to commit it openly and in full view while they looked on. And His saying ﴿Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women﴾, meaning: not for chastity and self-restraint, nor for offspring and procreation, but only to satisfy bestial lust; your condition is then like that of beasts and no more. At the same time you have harmed your women, since you have abandoned approaching them, thereby violating their rights. And His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Rather, you are a people who are ignorant﴾, meaning: Lut, peace be upon him, told them that this evil and corruption did not come from you except because you are a wicked people, ignorant of what is incumbent upon you toward your Lord in faith and obedience, and of what follows from disbelief and disobedience in the way of punishment and torment.

Lessons from the verses:

1- A clarification of the corruption and the intellectual and moral decline in which the people of Lut were.

2- The prohibition of the abomination of sodomy (liwat), that it is the most ugly thing, and that its perpetrator is baser than beasts.

3- A statement that ignorance of Allah the Exalted, of the obedience due to Him, and of His punishment and the lasting bliss with Him, is the cause of every evil and corruption on earth. Therefore the path to reforming mankind is to make them know Allah the Exalted, so that once they know Him and believe in Him, they can walk straight in life upon the method of reform that prepares for happiness and perfection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 56–58:

Explanation of the words:

*Fa-ma kana jawaba qawmihi*: That is, they had no answer except their saying, "Expel them."

*Al Lut* (the family of Lut): They are Lut (peace be upon him), his believing wife, and his two daughters.

*Min qaryatikum*: That is, from your town, Sodom (Sadum).

*Yatatahharun*: That is, they keep themselves pure and clean from filth and dirt.

*Qaddarnaha min al-ghabirin*: That is, We decreed that she should be among those who perish.

*Fa-sa'a matharu al-mundharin*: That is, evil was the rain of those warned, from among the people of crimes; it was stones of sijjil.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the remainder of the account of Lut (peace be upon him). After Lut (peace be upon him) denounced to his people the vile deed of sodomy (liwat), rebuked them for it, and condemned their act, they answered him with threats of expulsion and banishment from the town, as Allah the Exalted related: *"So the answer of his people was only that they said, 'Expel the family of Lut from your town.'"* That is, they had no answer with which to respond to Lut (peace be upon him) except their saying, ﴿Expel the family of Lut from your town﴾. They gave as the reason for this saying, ﴿Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, that is, they keep themselves clean of immoralities. They said this mockingly, not as an acknowledgment that the immorality is a filth from which one must keep oneself clean. When their transgression reached the point of threatening the Prophet of Allah, Lut (peace be upon him), with expulsion and mocking him, Allah the Exalted destroyed them and saved Lut and his family, except his wife, who was an old, disbelieving woman. This is the meaning of His saying in verse [57]: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; We decreed that she be among those who remained behind.﴾ That is, We decreed that she remain with the disbelievers to perish with them. As for His saying in verse [58]: ﴿And We rained upon them﴾, it explains the manner in which the people of Lut were destroyed: He rained upon them stones of sijjil, layered, and so destroyed them. ﴿So evil was the rain of those warned﴾, that is, evil was this rain from the rain of those warned, who denied what they were warned of and persisted in disbelief and sins. This rain came after Allah turned the high parts of their land to its low parts; He followed their sinking with a rain of stones so as to strike those who were far from the cities.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the sunnah that when wrongdoers are overcome by proofs and evidence, they resort to force.

2- Explanation of the sunnah that when a person persists in a bad word or deed, it ceases to appear bad to him.

3- The sunnah of Allah saving His friends and destroying His enemies after the warned persist in disbelief and sins.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 59–64:

Explanation of the words:

išṭafā (chose): i.e., He chose them to bear His message and convey His call.

Ālāhu khayr (Is God better?): i.e., for the one who worships Him.

Ḥadā'iq dhāt bahja (gardens of delightful beauty): i.e., gardens of pleasing appearance because of their greenery and flowers.

Ya'dilūn (they ascribe equals): i.e., they set up with their Lord others such as idols and images.

Ja'ala al-arḍa qarāran (He made the earth a stable abode): i.e., a firm settled place that does not move or shake with its inhabitants.

Wa ja'ala khilālahā anhāran (and made rivers flow through it): i.e., He made sweet rivers run through it for drinking and irrigation.

Wa ja'ala lahā rawāsiya (and set firm mountains upon it): i.e., mountains He anchored in it so that it does not move or tilt.

Bayna al-baḥrayn ḥājizan (a barrier between the two seas): i.e., a separator so that neither mixes with the other.

Wa yakshif al-sū' (and removes the evil): i.e., the harm, illness and other afflictions.

Qalīlan mā tadhakkarūn (little do you take heed): i.e., you are admonished only a little.

Bushran bayna yadayy raḥmatih (as good tidings before His mercy): i.e., heralds before the rain, since the winds go before and then the rain follows.

Amman yabda'u al-khalq thumma yu'īduh (Or who originates creation and then repeats it): i.e., He originates it in the wombs, then repeats it on the Day of Resurrection.

Hātū burhānakum in kuntum ṣādiqīn (Bring your proof, if you are truthful): i.e., bring your argument, if you are truthful, that alongside God there is another god who does what has been mentioned.

Meaning of the verses:

When God informed His Messenger of the destruction of the criminals and the salvation of the believers, He commanded His Messenger to praise Him for that, teaching him and his community that when a blessing is renewed for them, they should praise God for it, so that this is among its thanks. God the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "Praise be to God"﴾, i.e., attribution of beauty to God is due to Him by right.

﴿And peace upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾, namely, those He chose for His message and for conveying His call to His servants, that they might worship Him, thereby being perfected and made happy in both lives.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is God better, or what they associate?﴾, i.e., Is God the Creator, the Provider, the Sustainer, the Mighty, the Avenger on His enemies, the Honorer of His friends, better, or what they associate with Him? Worship of Him is better for the one who worships Him, or the worship of those they associate. Then His saying ﴿Or who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky﴾, i.e., for your need of it for washing, drinking and irrigation, ﴿and We caused to grow thereby gardens﴾, i.e., orchards enclosed by walls and barriers, ﴿of delightful beauty﴾, i.e., goodliness and loveliness. ﴿It was not for you to cause their trees to grow﴾, i.e., you were not able to make their trees grow. ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ No, by God. ﴿Nay, but they are a people who ascribe equals﴾, i.e., they associate idols with their Lord and make them equal to Him in worship. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who made the earth a stable abode﴾, i.e., a firm place that does not move with its inhabitants or shake with them so that they perish. ﴿And made rivers flow through its midst﴾, i.e., between its parts. ﴿And set firm mountains upon it﴾, i.e., mountains to hold it steady. ﴿And placed between the two seas﴾, the sweet and the salt, ﴿a barrier﴾, so that the salt does not mix with the sweet and spoil it.

﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ The answer: No, by God. ﴿Nay, but most of them do not know﴾. Had they known, they would not have associated God's creatures with Him. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him﴾, i.e., to remove his harm. ﴿And removes the evil﴾, i.e., drives it away; evil is what afflicts a person, such as illness, hunger, thirst, drought and barrenness. ﴿And makes you successors on the earth﴾, making one generation succeed another; thus the present is successor to the past and will itself be a predecessor to those who succeed it. ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ The answer: there is no god with God. ﴿Little do you take heed﴾, i.e., you are admonished only a little by what you hear and see of God's signs.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea﴾, by the stars at night and by the signs that indicate and direct you to your destinations during the day. ﴿Or who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾, i.e., who stirs up the winds and sends them to precede the rain and announce it? No one other than God. Is there then a god with God? The answer: No, no. God alone is the true God, and whatever else is besides Him is false.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾, He declared Himself free of the associating of the polytheists, who worship idols that neither originate nor restore, neither create nor provide, neither give nor withhold. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who originates creation, then repeats it﴾, i.e., from drops of semen in the wombs; then after its life He causes it to die, then He restores it, and this is the meaning of ﴿then repeats it﴾.

﴿Or who provides for you from the heaven﴾ with rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ with plants. The answer: God, then. ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ The answer: No, no. And even if you claim there are gods with God, ﴿Say: "Bring your proof"﴾, i.e., your arguments, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that anyone other than God does any of what has been mentioned in this noble context.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The obligation to praise God and thank Him when blessings are renewed, and praise of God is the head of gratitude.

2. The legitimacy of sending peace upon the prophets when they are mentioned; whoever mentions one of them should say, "peace be upon him."

3. Condemnation of shirk and of the polytheists.

4. Affirmation of tawhid by its many dazzling proofs.

5. Affirmation of the belief in the Last Resurrection and its establishment by inference from the proofs mentioned.

6. Rulings are established only by transmitted and rational evidence.

Ja'ala al-arḍa qarāran (He made the earth a stable abode): i.e., a firm settled place that does not move or shake with its inhabitants.

Wa ja'ala khilālahā anhāran (and made rivers flow through it): i.e., He made sweet rivers run through it for drinking and irrigation.

Wa ja'ala lahā rawāsiya (and set firm mountains upon it): i.e., mountains He anchored in it so that it does not move or tilt.

Bayna al-baḥrayn ḥājizan (a barrier between the two seas): i.e., a separator so that neither mixes with the other.

Wa yakshif al-sū' (and removes the evil): i.e., the harm, illness and other afflictions.

Qalīlan mā tadhakkarūn (little do you take heed): i.e., you are admonished only a little.

Bushran bayna yadayy raḥmatih (as good tidings before His mercy): i.e., heralds before the rain, since the winds go before and then the rain follows.

Amman yabda'u al-khalq thumma yu'īduh (Or who originates creation and then repeats it): i.e., He originates it in the wombs, then repeats it on the Day of Resurrection.

Hātū burhānakum in kuntum ṣādiqīn (Bring your proof, if you are truthful): i.e., bring your argument, if you are truthful, that alongside God there is another god who does what has been mentioned.

Meaning of the verses:

When God informed His Messenger of the destruction of the criminals and the salvation of the believers, He commanded His Messenger to praise Him for that, teaching him and his community that when a blessing is renewed for them, they should praise God for it, so that this is among its thanks. ﴿And peace upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾, namely, those He chose for His message and for conveying His call to His servants, that they might worship Him, thereby being perfected and made happy in both lives.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is God better, or what they associate?﴾, i.e., Is God the Creator, the Provider, the Sustainer, the Mighty, the Avenger on His enemies, the Honorer of His friends, better, or what they associate with Him? Worship of Him is better for the one who worships Him, or the worship of those they associate. Then His saying ﴿Or who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky﴾, i.e., for your need of it for washing, drinking and irrigation, ﴿and We caused to grow thereby gardens﴾, i.e., orchards enclosed by walls and barriers, ﴿of delightful beauty﴾, i.e., goodliness and loveliness. ﴿It was not for you to cause their trees to grow﴾, i.e., you were not able to make their trees grow. ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ No, by God. ﴿Nay, but they are a people who ascribe equals﴾, i.e., they associate idols with their Lord and make them equal to Him in worship. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who made the earth a stable abode﴾, i.e., a firm place that does not move with its inhabitants or shake with them so that they perish. ﴿And made rivers flow through its midst﴾, i.e., between its parts. ﴿And set firm mountains upon it﴾, i.e., mountains to hold it steady. ﴿And placed between the two seas﴾, the sweet and the salt, ﴿a barrier﴾, so that the salt does not mix with the sweet and spoil it.

﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ The answer: No, by God. ﴿Nay, but most of them do not know﴾. Had they known, they would not have associated God's creatures with Him. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him﴾, i.e., to remove his harm. ﴿And removes the evil﴾, i.e., drives it away; evil is what afflicts a person, such as illness, hunger, thirst, drought and barrenness. ﴿And makes you successors on the earth﴾, making one generation succeed another; thus the present is successor to the past and will itself be a predecessor to those who succeed it. ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ The answer: there is no god with God. ﴿Little do you take heed﴾, i.e., you are admonished only a little by what you hear and see of God's signs.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea﴾, by the stars at night and by the signs that indicate and direct you to your destinations during the day. ﴿Or who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾, i.e., who stirs up the winds and sends them to precede the rain and announce it? No one other than God. Is there then a god with God? The answer: No, no. God alone is the true God, and whatever else is besides Him is false.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾, He declared Himself free of the associating of the polytheists, who worship idols that neither originate nor restore, neither create nor provide, neither give nor withhold. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who originates creation, then repeats it﴾, i.e., from drops of semen in the wombs; then after its life He causes it to die, then He restores it, and this is the meaning of ﴿then repeats it﴾.

﴿Or who provides for you from the heaven﴾ with rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ with plants. The answer: God, then. ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ The answer: No, no. And even if you claim there are gods with God, ﴿Say: "Bring your proof"﴾, i.e., your arguments, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that anyone other than God does any of what has been mentioned in this noble context.

3. Condemnation of shirk and of the polytheists.

4. Affirmation of tawhid by its many dazzling proofs.

5. Affirmation of the belief in the Last Resurrection and its establishment by inference from the proofs mentioned.

6. Rulings are established only by transmitted and rational evidence.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 65–69:

Explanation of the words:

"Whoever is in the heavens and the earth": the angels and the humans.

"The unseen except Allah": that is, what is hidden from them, and among it, when the Hour will come, none knows except Allah, for He knows it.

"When they will be raised": that is, when they will be resurrected.

"Rather, their knowledge has overtaken them concerning the Hereafter": that is, it has followed on, and none of them has any certainty, so they have no knowledge of the Hereafter whatsoever.

"Rather, they are blind to it": that is, in complete blindness, they see nothing of its realities.

"When we are brought forth?": that is, alive from our graves.

"We and our fathers were promised this before": that is, the resurrection of the living from the graves.

"It is nothing but the fables of the former peoples": that is, their falsehoods which they wrote down in their books.

"See how was the end of the criminals": that is, the ones who denied the resurrection, their end was destruction and annihilation, and their desolate dwellings bear witness to this.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾. When the polytheists of Quraysh asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Hour, He commanded him to answer them with this reply: ﴿Say: None knows…﴾ etc. The Hour is among the unseen, rather it is the greatest of it. ﴿Whoever is in the heavens﴾ from the angels, ﴿and the earth﴾ from the humans, ﴿except Allah﴾ — that is, but Allah, may He be exalted, knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth; as for others, they know only what Allah has taught them, the Knower of the unseen.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾. That is, the people of the heavens and the people of the earth do not perceive when the dead will be raised from their graves for reckoning and recompense. This is like His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat al-A'raf:

﴿They ask you about the Hour, when will be its arrival? Say: Its knowledge is with my Lord alone. None will reveal its time except Him. It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly﴾ [Verse 187].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has overtaken them concerning the Hereafter﴾. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 70–75:

Explanation of the words:

"And do not grieve over them": the intended meaning is to console the Messenger (ﷺ).

"Of what they plot": that is, against you, when they tried to kill him and did not succeed.

"When is this promise": that is, of Our punishment.

"Some of what you are hastening": and it did happen to them at Badr.

"Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind": that is, in creating them, providing for them, preserving them, and not sending down punishment upon them.

"What their breasts conceal": that is, what their breasts hide and keep secret.

"And there is not an unseen thing": that is, there is no unseen event in the heaven and the earth except that it is in a clear record, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), recorded and written down in it.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the call of the polytheists to monotheism, belief in prophethood, and the Last Resurrection. The affirmation of the creed of monotheism has already been established with arguments that cannot be refuted, and likewise the affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense. But the polytheists continued to oppose, resist, and even plot. Therefore Allah the Exalted forbade His Messenger from grieving over the polytheists for their disbelief, just as He forbade him from distress at what they plot against him and against the true call that he calls to. This is what the first verse [70] indicates. As for the second and third verses, Allah the Exalted informs His Messenger of what his enemies say and teaches him the answer. Allah the Exalted says: [71] ﴿And they say, "When is this promise [of punishment], if you are truthful?"﴾ [72] ﴿Say, "Perhaps there has drawn near to you some of what you are impatient for."﴾ That is, it has come close to you and approached you, and it is what happened to them at Badr of captivity and killing. This is what the two verses [71 and 72] indicate.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, both believers and disbelievers, since He created them, provided for them, granted them well-being, and did not destroy them for their sins, ﴿but most of them do not give thanks﴾. Here they are, hastening the punishment and demanding it, and yet He gives them respite so that perhaps they will repent, and this is the greatest bounty. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare﴾, meaning nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, and He will record their deeds for them and recompense them for them. In this is consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and a warning and threat to them. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven and the earth but that it is in a clear record﴾, which is the Preserved Tablet; that is, the knowledge of your Lord encompasses everything and nothing escapes Him. This is a manifestation of the divine knowledge, which necessitates resurrection and recompense, for if His knowledge of creation were diminished, it would be permissible that He leave some of them unresurrected, unaccounted, and unrecompensed.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Consolation of the Messenger (ﷺ), for he suffers hardship from the wrongdoing and aversion of the polytheists.

2- Clarification of the obstinacy and stubbornness of the polytheists.

3- The fulfillment of Allah's promise to the polytheists, as some of the punishment they were hastening came upon them.

4- Clarification of Allah's bounty upon mankind, despite most of them not giving thanks to Him, glory be to Him.

5- Clarification of the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah over everything.

6- Affirmation and establishment of the Book of Decrees, which is the Preserved Tablet.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 76–81:

Explanation of the words:

"Yaqussu ʿala Bani Isra'il" (it relates to the Children of Israel): i.e., it mentions, in the course of its verses, much of what the Children of Israel differed over.

"Li-hudan wa rahmatan lil-mu'minin" (a guidance and a mercy for the believers): i.e., through it the guidance and mercy of the believers are completed.

"Yaqdi baynahum bi-hukmihi" (He judges between them by His judgment): i.e., He judges between the Children of Israel by His just judgment.

"Wa huwa al-ʿAziz al-ʿAlim" (And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing): the one who prevails over His affair, the one who knows His creation.

"Fa-tawakkal ʿala Allah" (So put your trust in Allah): i.e., have confidence in Him and entrust your affair to Him.

"Innaka la tusmiʿu al-mawta" (Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear): i.e., even if you wished to make them hear, because they are dead.

"Wa la tusmiʿu al-summa al-duʿa'" (Nor can you make the deaf hear the call): i.e., nor can you make the deaf, who have lost the sense of hearing, hear your speech.

"Idha wallaw mudbirin" (when they turn back, retreating): i.e., when they return, turning their backs on you, not paying attention to you.

"In tusmiʿu illa man yu'minu bi-ayatina" (You make none hear except those who believe in Our signs): i.e., you make none hear except those who believe in the signs of Allah.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an﴾, the Noble, which was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿relates to the Children of Israel﴾ who were contemporary with its revelation ﴿most of that about which they differ﴾, such as their differing concerning ʿIsa (peace be upon him) and his mother, for some exceeded the limits concerning them and deified them, while others fell short and said of ʿIsa that he was a sorcerer, and of Maryam that she was an adulteress, may Allah curse them; and such as their differing concerning the attributes of Allah the Exalted and the reality of the Return, and their differing over legal matters and other historical ones. The words of the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, it is a guidance and a mercy﴾, i.e., and indeed the Noble Qur'an is a guidance, meaning a guide for whoever believes in it to the path of peace, and a comprehensive mercy ﴿for the believers﴾ in it, who act upon what it contains of laws, manners and morals. The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, i.e., O Messenger, ﴿will judge between them﴾, i.e., between people, from polytheists and People of the Book, on the Day of Resurrection, with His just and merciful judgment, ﴿and He is the All-Mighty﴾, the one who prevails and whose judgment is executed upon whomever He judges for or against, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of the truthful from the falsifiers among His servants; therefore His judgment is most just and most merciful. And therefore ﴿So put your trust in Allah﴾, O Messenger, with confidence in Him and entrusting your affair to Him, for He is sufficient for you. The words: ﴿Indeed, you are upon the manifest truth﴾, i.e., indeed you, O our Messenger, are upon the true religion, which is Islam, and your opponents are upon falsehood, so the good outcome is yours, without doubt. The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾, and the disbelievers are dead through the absence of the spirit of faith in their bodies, and the dead do not hear; therefore you cannot make these dead disbelievers hear, just as you cannot make ﴿the deaf hear the call﴾, i.e., those who have lost the sense of hearing, ﴿your call﴾, ﴿when they turn back, retreating﴾, i.e., when they return, turning their backs, not paying attention to you. ﴿Nor can you guide the blind away from their error﴾ in which they live; so ease your soul, do not be distressed, and do not grieve. ﴿You make none hear except those who believe in Our signs﴾, i.e., you make none hear with understanding and acceptance except the believers in the signs of Allah, ﴿and they are Muslims﴾, i.e., they, because of their faith, are Muslims, meaning submissive and subject to the law of Allah and His rulings.

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of these verses:

1- The nobility and excellence of the Qur'an.

2- The disputes of the Jews and Christians will not end except through Islam; when they embrace Islam they will be guided to the truth and every dispute among them will end.

3- Every dispute among people today, Allah the Exalted will judge between its parties on the Day of Resurrection with His just judgment, and each will be given what is theirs or against them, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.

4- The disbelievers are dead, because their bodies are empty of the spirit of faith; therefore they do not hear guidance nor see the signs, however clear they may be.

So the one who calls them should recognize this in them, and be patient in his call and in their contentions.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verse 82–86:

Explanation of the words:

"And when the word has come to pass against them": that is, the punishment has become due for them.

"A creature from the earth": an animal that crawls upon the earth; its description has not been reported in any sound hadith that may be relied upon and affirmed.

"Speaks to them": in a language they understand, because it is one of the signs.

"That the people were not certain of Our signs": that is, because the people had come to not believe in the signs and laws of Allah, i.e., they disbelieved, and so they are tested by this creature.

"And [mention] the Day when We gather": that is, mention the day when We assemble.

"From every nation a company": that is, a group, namely the leaders who were followed in the worldly life.

"Then they will be driven": that is, they will be assembled, with the first of them being held back until the last of them arrives.

"Until, when they have come": that is, to the place of standing, the place of reckoning.

"And the word has come to pass against them": that is, the punishment has become due for them.

"Because of what they wronged": that is, because of the wrongdoing, which is their associating others with Allah, exalted is He.

"And they will not be able to speak": that is, they will have no proof.

"And the day [made] visible": that is, one sees in it for the sake of carrying out works.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, exalted is He: "And when the word has come to pass against them" means the punishment has become due for the disbelievers, since no one remains on earth who enjoins good or forbids evil. "We will bring forth for them" to test them, "a creature from the earth": an earthly animal, not a heavenly one. "Speaks to them": that is, in a language they understand. "That the people were not certain of Our signs": this is the reason for its speaking to them, namely that the people disbelieved and no longer became certain of the signs and laws of Allah, so Allah, exalted is He, brings forth this creature for wisdoms among which is that the believer is distinguished from the disbeliever by it. His saying, exalted is He: "And [mention] the Day when We gather from every nation a company": that is, mention, O Our Messenger, the day when We gather from every nation of the human nations a company, meaning a group, "of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven," with the first of them held back until the last of them arrives, so that their march is ordered. "Until, when they have come": the place of standing, the place of reckoning. Allah, exalted is He, says to them: "Did you deny My signs while you did not encompass them in knowledge?" This is a rebuke and reproach to them, for a person who has not encompassed knowledge of something is not permitted to deny it merely because he has not known it. His saying: "Or what was it that you were doing?" means what you were doing regarding My signs of affirmation and denial. He, exalted is He, says: "And the word has come to pass against them" means the punishment became due "because of their wrongdoing," that is, because of their wrongdoing, "so they will not be able to speak": that is, by their inability to defend themselves, because they were polytheists who wronged themselves.

His saying, exalted is He: "Do they not see" means: Do those polytheists who deny resurrection and recompense not see that Allah, exalted is He, made "the night for them to rest therein," and their resting is their death upon their beds through sleep in it, "and the day [made] visible," that is, made so that one sees in it, in order to go about in work for their livelihood. The sleep of the night resembles death, and the rising of the day resembles life; thus it is a process of repeated death and life throughout time, so how can the intelligent deny the final resurrection when it has a repeated form throughout life? Therefore He, exalted is He, said: "Indeed in that" — that is, in that repeated work of death and life every day and night — "are signs," that is, decisive proofs and evidences of the existence of a resurrection and life after this death and life.

The believers were singled out for mention and for attaining the required proof from the process of night and day, because the believers are living; they hear, see, and think, while the disbelievers are dead, and the dead do not hear, see, comprehend, or think.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the sign of the creature, which will come out from a cleft of al-Safa; the cleft now appears to exist, namely the tunnels that were opened in the mountain of al-Safa and became great roads for the pilgrims, and it will soon come out, on a day when no one remains who enjoins good or forbids evil, so the punishment becomes due for the disbelievers.

2- Establishing the creed of resurrection and recompense by mentioning its description.

3- Woe to the leaders of misguidance, evil, polytheism and falsehood, when they are brought forth and questioned.

4- In the sign of the night and day is clear indication of the creed of the final resurrection, reckoning and recompense.
