"Then they will be driven": that is, they will be assembled, with the first of them being held back until the last of them arrives.

"Until, when they have come": that is, to the place of standing, the place of reckoning.

"And the word has come to pass against them": that is, the punishment has become due for them.

"Because of what they wronged": that is, because of the wrongdoing, which is their associating others with Allah, exalted is He.

"And they will not be able to speak": that is, they will have no proof.

"And the day [made] visible": that is, one sees in it for the sake of carrying out works.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, exalted is He: "And when the word has come to pass against them" means the punishment has become due for the disbelievers, since no one remains on earth who enjoins good or forbids evil. "We will bring forth for them" to test them, "a creature from the earth": an earthly animal, not a heavenly one. "Speaks to them": that is, in a language they understand. "That the people were not certain of Our signs": this is the reason for its speaking to them, namely that the people disbelieved and no longer became certain of the signs and laws of Allah, so Allah, exalted is He, brings forth this creature for wisdoms among which is that the believer is distinguished from the disbeliever by it. His saying, exalted is He: "And [mention] the Day when We gather from every nation a company": that is, mention, O Our Messenger, the day when We gather from every nation of the human nations a company, meaning a group, "of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven," with the first of them held back until the last of them arrives, so that their march is ordered. "Until, when they have come": the place of standing, the place of reckoning. Allah, exalted is He, says to them: "Did you deny My signs while you did not encompass them in knowledge?" This is a rebuke and reproach to them, for a person who has not encompassed knowledge of something is not permitted to deny it merely because he has not known it. His saying: "Or what was it that you were doing?" means what you were doing regarding My signs of affirmation and denial. He, exalted is He, says: "And the word has come to pass against them" means the punishment became due "because of their wrongdoing," that is, because of their wrongdoing, "so they will not be able to speak": that is, by their inability to defend themselves, because they were polytheists who wronged themselves.

His saying, exalted is He: "Do they not see" means: Do those polytheists who deny resurrection and recompense not see that Allah, exalted is He, made "the night for them to rest therein," and their resting is their death upon their beds through sleep in it, "and the day [made] visible," that is, made so that one sees in it, in order to go about in work for their livelihood. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: "Indeed in that" — that is, in that repeated work of death and life every day and night — "are signs," that is, decisive proofs and evidences of the existence of a resurrection and life after this death and life.

The believers were singled out for mention and for attaining the required proof from the process of night and day, because the believers are living; they hear, see, and think, while the disbelievers are dead, and the dead do not hear, see, comprehend, or think.

3- Woe to the leaders of misguidance, evil, polytheism and falsehood, when they are brought forth and questioned.

4- In the sign of the night and day is clear indication of the creed of the final resurrection, reckoning and recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 87–90:

Explanation of the words:

"And the day the Trumpet is blown": that is, the day Israfil blows into the horn (al-buq), the blast of terror, annihilation, and rising from the graves.

"And all will come to Him humbled": that is, all who are in the heavens and the earth will come to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, humbled, abased, and submissive.

"And you see the mountains, thinking them solid": that is, you suppose them, by the eye's judgment, to be solid.

"Yet they pass by as the clouds pass": this is because of the speed of their movement.

"Whoever comes with a good deed": this is faith, monotheism, and all righteous deeds.

"He will have better than it": that is, Paradise.

"And whoever comes with an evil deed": that is, polytheism and sins, "they will be hurled face-first into the Fire" (yukabbu wajhahu fīhā).

"And they will be safe from the terror of that Day": that is, the possessors of the good deeds of monotheism and righteous action will be safe from the terror of the great horror of the Day of Resurrection.

"But whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be flung into the Fire": that is, whoever comes with an evil deed such as polytheism, consuming usury, or killing a soul, their faces will be flung into the Fire, may Allah protect us, that is, they will be cast into it upon their faces.

"Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?": that is, you are not recompensed except by your deeds, and you are not recompensed for the deeds of others.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of the events of the Resurrection, to establish the belief in resurrection and recompense, which is the motive for steadfastness in life. Allah, the Exalted, says: "And the day the Trumpet is blown" — that is, Israfil blows, by the leave of his Lord, into the Trumpet, which is the horn or the buq, "and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills." His saying, "And you see the mountains, thinking them solid": that is, they do not move, while in reality they move as the clouds move. "Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do": and He will recompense you, O people, according to His knowledge. "Whoever comes with a good deed": this is faith and righteous action. "He will have better than it": that is Paradise. "And whoever comes with an evil deed": this is polytheism and sins, "their faces will be flung into the Fire": that is the recompense of whoever comes with an evil deed.

His saying, the Exalted: "Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?": that is, you are not recompensed except for what you used to do in the world, of good and evil. The recompense has been completed accordingly: a group entered Paradise, and others had their faces flung into the Fire.

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense by describing its events in detail.

2- Explaining how the worlds will be ruined and the created order will pass away.

3- The virtue of the martyrs, for the greatest terror does not grieve them, and they are safe.

4- Establishing the principle of recompense: the good deed and the evil deed, the good deed being monotheism and the evil deed being polytheism.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 91–93:

Explanation of the words:

hadhihi al-baldah (this city): i.e., Makkah al-Mukarramah, and the attribution (idafah) is one of honour.

alladhi harramaha (the One who made it sacred): i.e., Allah, who made Makkah sacred, so that its grass may not be cut, its game may not be frightened, and no fighting may take place in it.

min al-muslimin (of those who submit): the believers who submit to Him outwardly and inwardly, and they are the noblest of creation.

wa an atluwa al-Qur'an (and that I recite the Qur'an): i.e., He commanded me to recite the Qur'an as a warning, as instruction, and as an act of worship.

sayurikum ayatihi (He will show you His signs): i.e., the referent of the signs of threat, so that they will know it. He showed it to them at Badr, and they will see it at death.

wa ma rabbuka bi-ghafilin 'amma ya'malun (and your Lord is not unaware of what you do): i.e., and your Lord, O Messenger, is not unaware of what people do, and He will recompense them for their deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

After that tremendous presentation of the events of the Resurrection, which everyone who witnessed it should have believed in, yet most of the people did not believe, there is a fitting explanation of the position of the Messenger ﷺ. He is a servant commanded to worship his Lord and no other. The Lord of this city, who made it sacred so that fighting in it is forbidden, its game may not be hunted, its grass may not be cut, and its lost property may not be picked up except by one who will announce it, is the One to whom belongs everything in creation, dominion, and disposal. Thus no other has any share with Him in all the worlds, the upper and the lower. His saying, ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾, means: my Lord has commanded me to be among the Muslims, that is, those who submit to Allah and humble themselves before Him, and they are the righteous servants of His, from among the prophets and messengers. His saying, ﴿And that I recite the Qur'an﴾, means: He commanded me to recite the Qur'an as a recitation of warning, instruction, worship, and drawing near to Him, exalted is He. After my recitation, whoever is guided and recognises the path of guidance and follows it, the fruits of guidance return to him, and he is the one who benefits from it. Whoever goes astray, does not accept guidance, and persists in his error, then it is not my responsibility to guide him, for my Lord has said to me: Say to those who go astray, ﴿I am only one of the warners﴾, not one who bestows faith and guidance. Rather, guidance is bestowed and granted by Allah, in whose hand is everything. ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah﴾: He commanded me to praise Him for every blessing He has bestowed upon me, countless and uncounted, and among the greatest of them is His honouring me with the message, by which He has favoured me over all people. So praise belongs to Allah, and the favour is His. His saying ﴿He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them﴾ means: and inform these polytheists that Allah, my Lord, will show you His signs in the future of your days. He showed them the first sign at Badr and the second sign at the Conquest, and the last sign at death, on the day when the angels strike their faces and their backs and say to them, ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 181]. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾ means: and your Lord, who has honoured and favoured you, O Messenger, ﴿is not unaware of what you do﴾, O people, whether believers or disbelievers, righteous or corrupt, and He will recompense each one for his deed on the day you return to Him. In the verse, then, there is both promise and warning.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the Messenger's ﷺ duty: it is worship of Allah and submission to Him, and reciting the Qur'an as warning, admonition, instruction, and worship of Him, and drawing near to the One who sent it down, exalted is He.

2- Explanation and affirmation of the sanctity of Makkah al-Mukarramah and the Sacred Precinct (haram).

3- Recommendation to praise Allah, exalted is He, for His outward and inward blessings, especially when a blessing is renewed and when it is mentioned.

4- Explanation that the fruits of one's earnings return to the earner, whether good or evil.

5- Explanation of the miracle of the noble Qur'an: it informed the polytheists that they would see its signs, and they did see them in fact, though it was unseen (ghayb); thus it came to pass as it had reported.

The Lord of this city, who made it sacred so that fighting in it is forbidden, its game may not be hunted, its grass may not be cut, and its lost property may not be picked up except by one who will announce it, is the One to whom belongs everything in creation, dominion, and disposal. Thus no other has any share with Him in all the worlds, the upper and the lower. His saying, ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾, means: my Lord has commanded me to be among the Muslims, that is, those who submit to Allah and humble themselves before Him, and they are the righteous servants of His, from among the prophets and messengers. His saying, ﴿And that I recite the Qur'an﴾, means: He commanded me to recite the Qur'an as a recitation of warning, instruction, worship, and drawing near to Him, exalted is He. After my recitation, whoever is guided and recognises the path of guidance and follows it, the fruits of guidance return to him, and he is the one who benefits from it. Whoever goes astray, does not accept guidance, and persists in his error, then it is not my responsibility to guide him, for my Lord has said to me: Say to those who go astray, ﴿I am only one of the warners﴾, not one who bestows faith and guidance. Rather, guidance is bestowed and granted by Allah, in whose hand is everything. ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah﴾: He commanded me to praise Him for every blessing He has bestowed upon me, countless and uncounted, and among the greatest of them is His honouring me with the message, by which He has favoured me over all people. So praise belongs to Allah, and the favour is His. His saying ﴿He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them﴾ means: and inform these polytheists that Allah, my Lord, will show you His signs in the future of your days. He showed them the first sign at Badr and the second sign at the Conquest, and the last sign at death, on the day when the angels strike their faces and their backs and say to them, ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 181]. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾ means: and your Lord, who has honoured and favoured you, O Messenger, ﴿is not unaware of what you do﴾, O people, whether believers or disbelievers, righteous or corrupt, and He will recompense each one for his deed on the day you return to Him. In the verse, then, there is both promise and warning.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the Messenger's ﷺ duty: it is worship of Allah and submission to Him, and reciting the Qur'an as warning, admonition, instruction, and worship of Him, and drawing near to the One who sent it down, exalted is He.

2- Explanation and affirmation of the sanctity of Makkah al-Mukarramah and the Sacred Precinct (haram).

3- Recommendation to praise Allah, exalted is He, for His outward and inward blessings, especially when a blessing is renewed and when it is mentioned.

4- Explanation that the fruits of one's earnings return to the earner, whether good or evil.

5- Explanation of the miracle of the noble Qur'an: it informed the polytheists that they would see its signs, and they did see them in fact, though it was unseen (ghayb); thus it came to pass as it had reported.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 27, verses 91–93:

Explanation of the words:

hadhihi al-baldah (this city): i.e., Makkah al-Mukarramah, and the attribution (idafah) is one of honour.

alladhi harramaha (the One who made it sacred): i.e., Allah, who made Makkah sacred, so that its grass may not be cut, its game may not be frightened, and no fighting may take place in it.

min al-muslimin (of those who submit): the believers who submit to Him outwardly and inwardly, and they are the noblest of creation.

wa an atluwa al-Qur'an (and that I recite the Qur'an): i.e., He commanded me to recite the Qur'an as a warning, as instruction, and as an act of worship.

sayurikum ayatihi (He will show you His signs): i.e., the referent of the signs of threat, so that they will know it. He showed it to them at Badr, and they will see it at death.

wa ma rabbuka bi-ghafilin 'amma ya'malun (and your Lord is not unaware of what you do): i.e., and your Lord, O Messenger, is not unaware of what people do, and He will recompense them for their deeds.
